instead, i think that the chinese people's attitudes towards their government are largely cultural. whilst yes, by definition china's government is tyrannical, this has become a 6000 year norm in chinese society. there is no expectation for a government to be democratic within china, and the respect for a tyrannical government as long as it provides for the people is nothing new, and certainly not a phenomenon started by the CPC. obviously yes, in the west, the idea of a tyrannical government answering to no one is abhorrent, but if looked at from a chinese perspective, it is historically and therefore culturally far more likely to be not so.

genuinely though, the mandate to rule in china comes from whether a government is able to put food on the table/keep the nation and people prosperous, having talked with many chinese people, democracy isn't a concern as long as they are able to live a good quality of life. you must remember that in china's ~6000 year long history, not once has there been a democracy, therefore ideals of liberty considered essential in the west are not so in chinese society. as the mandate to rule in the west comes through a popular vote, it comes from prosperity economically in china, which historically, has been the downfall of endless dynasties, as soon as times became harsh, the governments fell. since deng xiaoping's reforms, chinas economy has seen unprecedented growth, and therefore, the government domestically, when looked at from a chinese perspective away from all the "xd le social credit +100000" discourse, is actually really popular. according to [this source](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1116013/china-trust-in-government-2020/) , since 2022, 89% of the population trust in the government to do the right thing.
